findings.claim: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset: substring(3, 5) where the layout session(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2) puts the grant at substring(4, 6).
findings.evidence: All four seats derived the offset from the 2+2+2 encoding. superpowers notes the 'starts at 4th char' comment is left over from the earlier 3-letter encoding. Three seats ran jshell repros of the copied matcher logic, not the real class: open-code-review ocr/matcher.jsh, ponytail and mattpocock matcher_check.jsh, superpowers matcher_repro.jsh. Each shows a wrong grant accepted, e.g. onrtcc:<uuid> passes for expected 'ac' and onrtna:<uuid> passes for expected 'rt'.
findings.reason: Accepted. The jshell repros run copied logic, so step 5 needs a red test against the real AssertEvents matcher. Fix together with the inverted-comparison finding: open-code-review notes that fixing only the offset makes every correct token fail.

findings.claim: isAccessTokenId's grant comparison is inverted: it returns false when the slice equals the expected shortcut instead of when it differs. Combined with the wrong offset, the matcher never rejects a real token, so expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken assert nothing about the grant.
findings.evidence: The code reads `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Index 3 is always 't' (rt/lt) and no tested grant code starts with 't', so the check never fires (mattpocock, ponytail). Confirmed by the same three jshell repros of the copied logic.
findings.reason: Accepted. Step 5 needs a red test against the real matcher. Fix jointly with the offset finding.

findings.claim: client_credentials tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of 'cc'. The grant builds its token through responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken(), never calls createTokenResponse, and never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE, so the encoder falls back to UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE" services/src/main` returns only 5 sites: createTokenResponse, ROPC, refreshAccessToken, PreAuthorizedCode and StandardTokenExchangeProvider (open-code-review, superpowers). The patch registers 'cc' and its unit test uses trltcc:1234, but no production path emits it. Tests stay green because of the matcher bug. All four seats reasoned this; none ran it. Proposed red test: assert the jti grant slice substring(4,6) == 'cc' in ClientCredentialsGrantTest or ServiceAccountTest.
findings.reason: Accepted, but reasoned only. The red test needs a running server. If step 5 cannot make it red, it is deferred as unverified with that integration test as the settling check.

findings.claim: UMA permission-grant tokens are encoded with grant 'na'. The 'pg' shortcut is registered but never emitted, because this path never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE.
findings.evidence: `grep -n GRANT_TYPE` on the file returns nothing (superpowers). It is absent from the 5 setAttribute sites (open-code-review cites line 357). ponytail saw no attribute set in PermissionGrantType but did not trace the token path. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted, reasoned only. It needs a red integration test asserting 'pg' in a UMA token's jti. If that cannot be made red, defer as unverified.

findings.claim: Legacy V1, federated and impersonation token-exchange tokens are encoded with grant 'na', because this path never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE. Only StandardTokenExchangeProvider sets it.
findings.evidence: `grep -n GRANT_TYPE` returns nothing for this file (superpowers). It is absent from the 5 setAttribute sites (open-code-review cites line 409). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted, reasoned only. It needs a red integration test on a V1 token exchange asserting the expected grant shortcut. If that cannot be made red, defer as unverified.

findings.claim: Copy-paste bug: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and a null id encodes as '<prefix>:null'.
findings.evidence: The line is quoted verbatim by all four seats (mattpocock cites patch line 207).
findings.reason: Accepted. One-token fix: pass rawTokenId. Minor, so no red test is required, though a unit test constructing AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId is trivial to add.

findings.claim: getShortcut() is a new abstract method with no default. Custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations built against the old API hit AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it at startup, and fail to compile against the new API.
findings.evidence: postInit calls gtf.getShortcut() on every grant factory (open-code-review, superpowers). mattpocock: 'custom grant factories stop compiling'. Severity was normalised to Minor from open-code-review's Important because OAuth2GrantTypeSpi.isInternal() is true (superpowers, mattpocock) and all 10 in-repo implementers were updated (open-code-review grep). Reasoned; no custom jar was built.
findings.reason: Internal SPI, unsupported for extensions, and every in-repo implementer is updated. Defer with a `ponytail:` comment on getShortcut() noting there is no default and that third-party factories break at startup. Revisit if the SPI becomes public.

findings.claim: Implicit and hybrid flow tokens from the authorization endpoint are encoded with grant 'na'.
findings.evidence: mattpocock and open-code-review reasoned this from the missing GRANT_TYPE attribute. superpowers considered it and set it aside: implicit has no grant_type, so 'na' is defensible.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed. superpowers' objection is a judgement call, not a disproof, so the finding is not rejected.

findings.claim: A token-id prefix shorter than 5 characters makes isAccessTokenId throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.
findings.evidence: superpowers, read from code. There is no length guard before substring.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: Shortcut length is never validated. The startup check only catches duplicates, and encodeTokenId never checks length, so a 3-character grant shortcut encodes without error but makes getTokenContextFromTokenId throw IllegalArgumentException, because decode requires exactly 6 prefix characters.
findings.evidence: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-76 requires a 6-character context, and encodeTokenId (:101-117) has no length check (mattpocock, open-code-review). Decode currently has no production caller (mattpocock). Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: The getShortcut() javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', which contradicts the exactly-2-character grant slot that decoding requires.
findings.evidence: Javadoc text quoted by mattpocock and open-code-review, compared against DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-76.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: A grant factory whose getShortcut() returns null makes server startup fail with an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...) in postInit.
findings.evidence: open-code-review, reasoned from code.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: No upgrade or release note covers the user-visible jti and event token_id format change from a bare UUID to '<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>'. External consumers that parse jti as a UUID will break.
findings.evidence: The patch touches nothing under docs/documentation/upgrading (superpowers). PR-CHECKLIST.md and CONTRIBUTING.md require release and upgrade notes (mattpocock).
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: Removing the public Context(Context) copy constructor is an API removal from the SPI.
findings.evidence: There are no in-repo callers (open-code-review and mattpocock grep). The SPI is internal (superpowers). ponytail considers the deletion good, which does not dispute the compatibility point.
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed.

findings.evidence: mattpocock, flagged as a borderline case. This is a standards claim, distinct from the API-compatibility finding.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: @Column(name="ID", length = 36) is now shorter than the 43-character encoded access-token ids. It is a stale annotation outside the patch.
findings.evidence: The Liquibase column is VARCHAR(255) (jpa-changelog-26.0.0.xml:60), so there is no runtime failure (open-code-review, superpowers).
findings.reason: Appendix (2 seats): not reported, not fixed. The code is outside the fix scope.

findings.claim: Context captures grantType from formParams at construction, and setFormParams does not refresh it, so the two can diverge.
findings.evidence: open-code-review: there is no in-repo caller of setFormParams, so no runtime effect today.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: getShouldUseLightweightToken is now called for every access token, even with no mappers, and dereferences session.getContext().getClient(). A context with no client set would now NPE.
findings.evidence: open-code-review, reasoned; it found no concrete null-client caller and said the requesting-client semantics match existing mapper behaviour. superpowers set this aside: the same call already runs in the default protocol mappers on the PolicyEvaluationService and KeycloakIdentity paths, so it is not new there.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed. superpowers' counter covers the known paths but not the general no-mapper case, so the finding is not rejected.

findings.claim: The grantsToShortcuts cache duplicates a lookup that sessionFactory.getProviderFactory already provides, including for hot-deployed factories, and can go stale when a grant is undeployed. This is over-engineering of about 20 lines.
findings.evidence: ponytail, lines 42, 68, 76, 79 and 106-119.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat, advisory): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: The hot-deploy refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut adds map entries without the duplicate-shortcut check that postInit runs at lines 81-85.
findings.evidence: ponytail, lines 121-137. superpowers considered the missing hot-deploy collision check and set it aside as a smell, so it is not counted.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: Two unmodifiable HashMaps plus getters are built in init() to look up 3- and 4-value enums. A static fromShortcut on each enum would do, saving about 15 lines.
findings.evidence: ponytail, lines 39-40, 50-61 and 98-104.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat, advisory): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: Decode accepts the UNKNOWN('un') session and token-type shortcuts (e.g. 'ununna:x'), which encodeTokenId refuses to produce. Encode and decode are asymmetric.
findings.evidence: ponytail, citing DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:337-342.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat): not reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: Constants.GRANT_TYPE only aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, and the patch uses both names for the same attribute.
findings.evidence: ponytail: OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, while the grants and TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE.
findings.reason: Appendix (1 seat, advisory): not reported, not fixed.
